transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with constant, uncontrollable worry and anxiety about many different things in my life. It has been going on for about two years now, and I just can't seem to stop it.
Along with the worry, have you been feeling down or depressed most days, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? If so, has that been happening for at least two weeks?
No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or have lost interest in my hobbies. My main struggle is just this constant, overwhelming worry that I can't seem to turn off, rather than feeling down or sad.
Did this anxiety start after a specific stressful life event or major change, or did it come on without one clear trigger? Has it continued even when that stressor was over or less intense?

I honestly can't recall any specific stressful life event or major trigger that started this. It just seemed to come on without a clear reason, and it has been ongoing continuously for about two years now.
With this ongoing worry, have you also had symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, trouble concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, or sleep problems?

I definitely struggle a lot with my concentration and focus, because my worries constantly intrude and disrupt my thoughts when I'm trying to get things done. However, I haven't really experienced or noticed the other things you mentioned, like restlessness, muscle tension, or sleep problems.

Before this anxiety started, did you already have long-standing problems with attention, organization, or forgetfulness going back to childhood or the teen years, across settings like school, home, or work?

No, I haven't really had any long-standing issues with attention, organization, or forgetfulness dating back to my childhood or teenage years. Those difficulties only started recently because my mind is constantly flooded with worries.
Over these two years, have you been worrying more days than not for at least six months, about several different areas of life such as work, health, finances, or family?

Yes, definitely. I've been worrying almost every single day for the entire two years this has been going on. It isn't just about one specific thing either; my anxiety constantly shifts between my work, family, finances, and other everyday matters.
How much is this anxiety interfering with your daily life, like your work, relationships, or ability to handle everyday tasks?

It is interfering with my daily life a lot because the worries are constantly intruding into my mind, making it really hard to focus at work and home. Since my anxiety spreads to almost everything—like work, family, and finances—it feels completely overwhelming. It really prevents me from functioning normally on a day-to-day basis.
Have these anxiety symptoms been related to any substance or medication use, like caffeine, stimulants, alcohol, or drugs, or to a medical problem such as thyroid issues?
No, I don't use any drugs or consume excessive caffeine or alcohol. Also, as far as I know, I don't have any underlying medical conditions, like thyroid issues, that could be causing these symptoms.
Do your worries mainly come as sudden panic attacks or from one specific fear, or are they more ongoing and spread across many parts of your life?

My worries are definitely more ongoing and spread across many different areas of my life, like my work, family, and finances, rather than being focused on one specific fear. I don't really experience sudden panic attacks; it is more of a constant, daily anxiety that is always in the background.
